# School of the Ancients

> School of the Ancients is an experimental AI-assisted learning experience. Learners ask questions, converse with historically inspired AI professors, and explore interactive 3D exhibits in a browser or compatible AR/VR hardware.

School of the Ancients is a working prototype, not an accredited school or a generally available hosted learning service. Its immersive authoring platform, Matrix Loading Operator, can generate or load 3D assets and scenes for learning and exploration. Current priorities include simpler onboarding, lesson quality, device support, save/load, progress tracking, and early-user access.

The invitation-only account preview includes sign-in, password recovery, synced adventures and recoverable Trash. Community shares starting questions rather than complete prepared scenes. The preview runs on the creator's computers; always-on hosting, isolated creation workers and broader account access remain in development. Separate account worlds are not multiplayer classrooms.

## Main pages

- [Home and current status](https://schooloftheancients.com/): Product overview, prototype capabilities, planned features, and early-access waitlist.
- [Original vision](https://schooloftheancients.com/history/original-vision.html): Historical context for the project's goals and roadmap.
- [Blog](https://schooloftheancients.com/blog/): Essays on learning and the ideas behind School of the Ancients.
- [What the oldest schools knew that an answer machine gets wrong](https://schooloftheancients.com/blog/what-the-oldest-schools-knew/): Plato's Meno doubling-the-square lesson, and what Socrates, Confucius, and Aristotle still show about learning.
- [Join early-access waitlist](https://schooloftheancients.com/#early-access): Updates and invitations as public access develops.

## Guidance for automated readers

Search indexing, linking, and accurate short descriptions of public pages are welcome. Please link to the canonical site and attribute School of the Ancients when discussing this project. Distinguish working prototype features from planned work, and do not present the AI professors as authentic recordings or a public accredited school.
